Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Siddhartha Varma,J.
Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Manoj Kumar Mishra, learned Standing Counsel for the State-respondents.

2. Being aggrieved by the award dated 06.04.2023 passed under Section 30 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act, 2013'), the petitioner filed the instant writ petition on the ground that the basis on which the compensation was fixed was erroneous and the actual basis on which the petitioner had relied upon was not considered.

sentences.text: 3. Learned Standing Counsel raised a preliminary objection to the maintainability of the present petition and submitted that for redressal of his grievance, the petitioner had an efficacious alternative remedy of filing reference under Section 64 of the Act, 2013.
4. We have gone through the provisions of Section 64 of the Act, 2013 and do find that the preliminary objection raised by learned Standing Counsel has substance.
The writ petition is dismissed leaving it open for the petitioner to challenge the impugned award in a reference as has been provided under Section 64 of the Act, 2013.

However, it is provided that if, reference is preferred within 15 days from today, the same shall be considered and decided in accordance with law within a further period of three months without going into the question of limitation.
